newsitem.title: USA: 22 U.S. states settle with Liggett on tobacco.
newsitem.headline: 22 U.S. states settle with Liggett on tobacco.

text.p: In a harsh blow to the tobacco industry, almost half of the nation's state attorneys general reached a settlement on Thursday with the Liggett Group to end lawsuits aimed at recouping health care costs of smokers.

The historic accord calls for unprecedented concessions from Liggett, owned by Bennet LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd., that include turning over evidence that could hurt the entire tobacco industry and placing warning labels on cigarette packages that smoking can be addictive.

Liggett also agreed to pay to the 22 settling states 25 percent of its pre-tax profits for the next 25 years to settle claims, according to the agreement announced at a news conference by the state attorneys-general.

The settlement marks the first time that a tobacco company has ever admitted that nicotine is addictive. In 1994 the heads of the major cigarette companies testified before Congress that nicotine is not addictive.
The Justice Department is currently conducting a criminal investigation into the industry in several areas including whether those executives lied.

The accord may also prove damaging to the industry because the documents involved might be used in the mounting litigation against cigarette companies and former and current Liggett employees may be called to testify.
